domain_restrictions: j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1
x is a real number with x in I_{n,j}
d is a real number satisfying 0 <= d < 1/n
the claimed witness satisfies d = x - j/n, so x - j/n must lie in [0, 1/n)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n and every integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, for every real x in I_{n,j}, there exists a unique real d such that 0 <= d < 1/n, x equals J_{n,j}(d), and this unique d is exactly x - j/n.
quantifier_order: for all integers j with 0 <= j <= n - 1
for all real x in I_{n,j}
there exists exactly one real d in [0, 1/n) such that x = J_{n,j}(d) and d = x - j/n

The fact that d lies in [0, 1/n) imposes the implicit requirement x in I_{n,j} implies 0 <= x - j/n < 1/n

statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. For every real x in I_{n,j}, there is exactly one real d in [0, 1/n) such that x = J_{n,j}(d), namely d = x - j/n.
